<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915018_theRebbe_923" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915018_theRebbe_923__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening header for the maamar, including the Torah portion and date.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbat Parshat Chayei Sarah,</t>
    <t s="2">Erev Rosh Chodesh Kislev, 5737.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the verse "And Avraham was old, advanced in days, and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything," and questions the meaning of "everything" as a hidden, boundless source.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And Avraham was old, advanced in days, and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything."</t>
    <t s="1">And the Rebbe [the Rebbe Rashab]</t>
    <t s="2">(the Rebbe Shalom Ber)</t>
    <t s="3">of blessed memory, in his maamar beginning with this discourse</t>
    <t s="4">(from the year 5666),</t>
    <t s="5">precisely notes that it says "with everything" in a general way, and does not specify with what He blessed him.</t>
    <t s="6">And the point of the explanation:</t>
    <t s="7">"Everything" is the aspect of the essential concealment,</t>
    <t s="8">from which all revelations are drawn.</t>
    <t s="9">As it is brought in the Zohar</t>
    <t s="10">on the verse "And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything,"</t>
    <t s="11">that Avraham was blessed from the place from which all blessings emanate.</t>
    <t s="12">Therefore it says "with everything" in a general way and does not specify details,</t>
    <t s="13">because it is the aspect of the boundless, which is above details.</t>
    <t s="14">And one must understand the connection and relevance of the Zohar's interpretation that "everything" is the place from which all blessings emanate, with Rashi's commentary on the verse,</t>
    <t s="15">that "everything" refers to Yitzchak</t>
    <t s="16">("everything" in gematria equals "ben" [son]).</t>
    <t s="17">And also,</t>
    <t s="18">from the continuation of the verses it seems that this verse</t>
    <t s="19">("And Avraham was old, etc.")</t>
    <t s="20">is an introduction to "And Avraham said to his servant, etc., 'And you shall take a wife for my son, for Yitzchak.'"</t>
    <t s="21">And one must understand what is the connection of "And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything,"</t>
    <t s="22">that he was blessed from the place from which all blessings emanate,</t>
    <t s="23">to this—that he sent his servant to take a wife for his son.</t>
    <t s="24">Also, one must understand the greatness of the elevation of the marriage of Yitzchak and Rivkah, that it is loftier even than the aspect of "everything"</t>
    <t s="25">(the place from which all blessings emanate),</t>
    <t s="26">to the point that this—that Hashem blessed Avraham with everything—is only an introduction to the marriage of Yitzchak and Rivkah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Avraham's ten trials correspond to the ten Sefiros, while "everything" refers to the innermost aspect of Kesser, which is beyond human arousal.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what is brought in the Midrash:</t>
    <t s="2">"The Holy One, blessed be He, does not elevate a person to greatness until He tests and examines him, etc. And so you find with Avraham our father: the Holy One, blessed be He, tested him with ten trials, and he withstood them, and afterwards He blessed him, as it is said, 'And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything.'"</t>
    <t s="3">And the Tzemach Tzedek explains,</t>
    <t s="4">that the ten trials correspond to the ten Sefiros,</t>
    <t s="5">whereas "everything" is the innermost aspect of Kesser, which is not</t>
    <t s="6">included in the count of the ten Sefiros.</t>
    <t s="7">For in that aspect,</t>
    <t s="8">no arousal from below reaches there.</t>
    <t s="9">And after Avraham withstood the ten trials corresponding to the ten Sefiros, in which arousal from below is relevant,</t>
    <t s="10">then He blessed him with "everything,"</t>
    <t s="11">the innermost aspect of Kesser.</t>
    <t s="12">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="13">that this is also the precise language of the verse: "And Avraham was old, advanced in days, and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything"—</t>
    <t s="14">that this—that he was old, advanced in days,</t>
    <t s="15">even though it is a blessing from the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="16">the verse attributes it to Avraham</t>
    <t s="17">("And Avraham was old, advanced in days"),</t>
    <t s="18">whereas regarding "everything," it does not say that Avraham had "everything," but rather that "Hashem blessed Avraham with everything."</t>
    <t s="19">The explanation of this can be said:</t>
    <t s="20">That which he was blessed with old age and days is an arousal from above that is aroused and drawn down by means of an arousal from below,</t>
    <t s="21">the service of Avraham,</t>
    <t s="22">whereas that which he was blessed with "everything" is an arousal from above that comes from above, to which no arousal from below reaches.</t>
    <t s="23">[And that this blessing came specifically after he withstood the ten trials is because there must be a place</t>
    <t s="24">that is complete],</t>
    <t s="25">therefore it is written regarding it, "And Hashem blessed, etc."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
